result.title: CaLA: Causal Latent Adjustment for World Models under Adaptive Policies
result.summary: World models is answering ``imagine" answers to ``what-if'' questions via imagined rollouts. But rollouts collected by adaptive policies induce treatment-outcome confounding in imagined rollouts. We study this problem in Match-3 difficulty adjustment, where latent player skill influences both assigned difficulty and churn. We build a fully specified Match-3 SCM with sequential mechanics, adaptive assignment, and paired ground-truth interventions, on which unadjusted models fit to the logged trajectories select difficulty settings that raise churn. We then introduce Causal Latent Adjustment (CaLA), a DAG-constrained world model that infers a variational player representation from pretreatment history. Across our evaluations, CaLA provides the most reliable population-level intervention estimates and competitive individualized decisions, although rich handcrafted histories can remain advantageous for individual-level adjustment. We further find that residual correction can degrade causal decision quality despite improving predictive fit, highlighting the need to distinguish predictive accuracy, confounding adjustment and the behavior of downstream causal estimators.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究自适应策略下世界模型 imagined rollout 中的处理—结果混杂问题，在 Match-3 难度调整场景构建含序贯机制与配对真实干预的 SCM 基准，并提出 DAG 约束的变分潜在表征模型 CaLA，从干预前历史推断玩家技能以改进人群级干预估计。
